recipes.name: Pasta, Broccoli and Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boneless chicken breast halves, cooked and chopped

steps.text: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta until al dente; drain.
Meanwhile, blanch broccoli in boiling water; remove with a slotted spoon and set aside.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add minced garlic and pesto; sauté for 2 minutes. Stir in chopped tomatoes; set aside.
In a large bowl, toss cooked pasta with broccoli, cooked chicken, and tomato mixture. Add grated Parmesan cheese, salt, and ground black pepper; mix well and serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Pasta, Broccoli and Chicken
raw_recipe.description: Tomatoes and pesto add zesty flavor to blanched broccoli tossed with chicken and pasta. A generous amount of Parmesan cheese completes the dish!

review.reviewBody:
So tastey!! We loved this pasta!! I cubed the chicken before cooking it, and then I cooked it in a frying pan with a little olive oil, lemon juice, and garlic powder which gave the chicken a nice flavor. 

I suggest starting the boiling water right away like the recipe says. I waited a little while and forgot how long it does take for water to boil, and then you can time it so the pasta is done at the same time as the sauce.

I followed other reviewers' suggestions and added a third tablespoon of pesto and that seemed like a great amount. We love tomatoes so next time I would add more. GREAT recipe!

Great base recipe. Next time I'll double the garlic, pesto and broccoli. I added capers, artichoke quarters, chopped greek olives and mushrooms. I reserved some juice from canned artichokes to loosen it a tad. As leftovers I added some chicken stock to loosen it again.

I made this but didn't have all the ingredients. So, I made a few changes and TADA! Instant yummy!

Started up the trusty cast iron skillet (16") and added about 2 teaspoons veggie oil (I was out of olive oil) and set to low.

Threw in 4 heaping tablespoons of ground garlic, a cut up green onion, chopped fresh broccoli, chopped carrots, and chopped celery. Added half a tomato, chopped. Added about a half cup chopped orange pepper.

Added basil, kosher salt, red and green pepper. Added a dash of onion salt.

Cooked low and slow, stirring occasionally for 20 or so minutes.

While the veggies cooked, I found half a pound of egg noodles and started them cooking in a separate pot; drained.

Once I thought the veggies were cooked through, I added half a pint of half & half and about a cup of milk. Then added about a cup of Mozzarella/Colby Jack cheese. Stirred until creamy.

Added cooked pasta and mixed thoroughly.

In the end, nothing was left and my 7yo licked his plate clean. I'll take that as a success! :)

Pasta, Broccoli & Chicken Haiku: "This was colorful. A vibrant and tasty dish. But More Pesto Please!" I should've taken the advice of other reviewers and up'ed the pesto b/c it was just a dainty kiss of flavor. I used more broccoli and less pasta (penne's all that I had, but hey, they're tubes too), and I also sauteed onion and bell pepper w/ the garlic. I also used an Italian-seasoned can of tomatoes as opposed to chopped fresh. I don't think that I changed the recipe too terribly much, so I'm only giving it 4 stars b/c I think 1.) Needs the onion inclusion, or at least more veggies & less noodle. 2.) Definitely needs more pesto and 3.) No wait, just the 2. It's a good meal and all the better that it's not a heavy-creamy-pesto dish, so the brightness of color and flavor is a nice harmony with the "healthy" fats of the oil and pesto.

This recipe had everything in it that I like in a grown-up meal. I used 5 cloves of minced garlic, 5 TB of pesto, and only about 1/8 of a cup of olive oil. I too cooked the broccoli in the pasta water for about 5 minutes, then removed. The thing about this recipe is that half of my dinner guests were my own picky children, and it was easy to remove some plain pasta, brocolli, and chicken before adding the Pesto sauce. They LOVED the rigatoni -- and my daughter even commented on how she loved the taste (never told her I had snuck some "Green sauce" onto a few of her noodles.) Everyone got something they loved.

I do love this recipe, but after I had made a few changes. There are some people that say it didn't have enough flavor and as the recipe sits yes I agree. What I did for the chicken was cook it in a pan in an asian salad dressing until done. Then cubed it and set it aside. The broccoli and tomatoes I used a lot more since I love vegetables. I used double the tomatoes and almost 2 full heads of broccoli. I used an entire tub of pesto (biutoni) and also doubled the parmesan. There's just too much pasta for the rest of the ingredients that the recipe calls for. I do like the recipe, but if followed to the T it isn't as good as it would be if you did it the way i did. Hope this helps!

This was amazing. The only thing I did differently was that I cooked my chicken on the BBQ (seasoned the chicken), and instead of using a fresh tomato (I didn't have one), I used a can of rotelle tomatoes with green chilies. I also took others advice and used more pesto (2 heaping tbsps. full) and I chose to use about 6 cloves of garlic. This is a keeper and I will be making it for our next lunch club at work! Can't wait to share it!

Sooo YUMMY!!! This has a vibrant flavor and it is a meal in itself. I prepped my chicken by baking it with some garlic salt and pepper, about 20 minutes at 400. I used twice as much pesto as called for and followed everything else. I let the chicken sit for 10 minutes and cubed it while the pasta was cooking. I threw my broccoli in with the pasta and made sure to heavily salt the water. I was a little worried about the sauce because it looked so oily but after adding in the parmesan it was just right. I even added the chicken drippings for a little more sauce. Really, this is one of the best pasta dishes and it's a nice change from red or cream sauces. I think salting the pasta water and making sure the chicken was well seasoned ensured it was not bland. Thank you so much for this one!

Sooo easy. Made with penne, canned diced tomatoes, frozen broccoli florets, 2 cloves garlic and a little bit of olive oil, then topped with shredded parmesan cheese. 1. Cook broccoli (about 3 min in boiling water) set aside 2. Bring water for penne to a boil, while sauteeing garlic and tomatoes in olive oil. 3. Drain Penne, place in bowl with broccoli then coat with tomato/garlic/olive oil mixture, toss 4. Sprinkle with parm. cheese and serve.

This was great. I chopped and added one zucchini and two yellow squash (crookneck) and sauted them for around 10 minutes in with the minced garlic and pesto sauce. I used the veggie rigatoni pasta (also known as Wacky Mac). Added 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes for just a little bit of warmth.

Great dinner and easy to make. I followed the advice of others and doubled broccoli, garlic, tomatoes and pesto. I also added red red peppers and onions. Seasoned the chicken with salt and pepper and cooked it with oil and garlic then added pesto, more garlic, peppers, onions and tomoatoes. Cooked the broccoli for 2 minutes with pasta. Family loved it , will definitely make again.

Went according to recipe. Tasted a bit bland to us. I'll make it again, but with some additions like an extra can of diced tomatoes and some added spices. It's a good basic dish that could use some modifications.

Too dry. Would be better with some chicken broth added. My hubby put salsa on it as was really dry for him. Delicious & tasty though. I add such dried tomatoes and mushrooms as well. Would use less pasta next time.
This was fantastic! I added more pesto as others suggested and it was great. Thanks for the recipe!
More sauce!
Loved it!! But there’s a little too much pasta, so I think next time I’ll use like 2/3 of the pasta needed and it’ll be perfect!
Felt this was lacking flavor. Added a little extra pesto which helped some, but would not make again.
Good easy recipe. Will most likely make it again using more pesto. I added some fresh basil and extra garlic since I used up the pesto I had.
I used Mexican sausages instead of chicken and a can of diced tomatoes. Delicious!
Flavor was good, but would use double the tomato next time.
